children: New Delhi, Nov. 15 -- Public sector lender, the Indian Overseas Bank (IOB) has increased interest rates on 444-day term deposits up by 15 basis points (bps), with effect from 10 November, the bank said in a statement.
Further, non-callable deposits will now earn 6.85%; while rates for callable and NRE (non-resident external) deposits revised to 6.75% each, the release added.
IOB this week raised interest rates on its 444-day term deposits by up to 15 bps, following a review by the bank's Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO).

Founded in February 1937, IOB was one of the 14 major banks nationalised by the Indian Government in 1969. It currently has a strong domestic presence with 3,542 branches and around 3,729 ATMs. The bank also provides services in Singapore, Hong Kong, Thailand, and Sri Lanka, with a Trust of more than 4.6 crore active customers, according to the release.
For the quarter ended 30 September 2026, the bank's operating profit was Rs.3,016 crore, and the net profit was Rs.1,912 crore, it added.
